newsitem.title: JAPAN: Nippon Oil to slash 30 bln yen costs by 1999/2000.
newsitem.headline: Nippon Oil to slash 30 bln yen costs by 1999/2000.

text.p: Japan's leading refiner Nippon Oil Co Ltd said on Tuesday that it would try to slash costs by 30 billion yen by the end of 1999/2000 business year by streamlining distribution and cutting personnel costs.
Nippon Oil has already closed six of its 18 branch offices in Japan and plans to gradually reduce its workforce to 3,600 from the current 4,200, a company spokesman said.
Next calendar year, Nippon Oil will start rationalising storage facilities, he said.
Earlier this year, as part of their efforts to cut distribution costs, Nippon Oil and rival refiner Idemitsu Kosan Co Ltd started supplying each other with fuel oil.
The oil industry has been hit hard by slumping retail prices of oil products after deregulation of imports this April.
Higher costs, due to surging crude oil prices and the yen's weakness against the dollar, are also eating away at oil firms' profits.
